Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 21529 of 2023

Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Devesh Kumar Sharma

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Anish Kumar Gupta,J.
1.

Heard Shri Devesh Kumar Sharma, learned counsel for the applicants and Shri Rakesh Soni, State Law Officer for the State.
2. The instant application U/S 482 Cr.P.C has been filed seeking quashing of the charge-sheet No.184/2022, dated 26.6.2022 against the applicants along with cognizance order dated 13.10.2022 and entire criminal proceeding of Criminal Case No.552 of 2022 (State Vs. Nitesh and others)
arising out of Case Crime No.143 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 323 IPC & 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Farah, District Mathura, pending in the Court of learned Civil Judge (J.D.), Fast Track Court ( Crime Against Women) Judicial Magistrate, Mathura.

entities.text: Fast Track Court ( Crime Against Women) Judicial Magistrate, Mathura
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the applicants submits that the instant case has been registered due to matrimonial discord between the applicants and daughter of opposite party no.2 and the said case was lodged on the basis of false and fabricated facts.

Therefore, prayer for quashing of the said case Nitesh And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 17 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193498655/
1 is made.

entities.text: Nitesh And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. On query made by the Court to the learned counsel for the applicants, the FIR and charge-sheet do not disclose any offence against the applicants herein.

5. Learned counsel for the State submits that the allegation made in the FIR has been duly supported by the witnesses in their statements recorded under section 161 Cr.P.C., therefore, there is no illegality in the charge-sheet or in the summoning order dated 13.10.2022.
6. Having heard the rival submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties, this Court has carefully perused the record of the case.

From perusal of the FIR, charge-sheet as well as statement of the witnesses recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C., it cannot be said that no offence as alleged in the FIR is made out against the applicants herein.
7. In view thereof, the instant application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. is dismissed.

8. Learned counsel for the applicants further submits that the matter be referred for mediation before the Mediation Centre of District Court, Mathura, so that the dispute between the parties can be resolved.

entities.text: Mediation Centre of District Court, Mathura
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
9. In view thereof, the applicants are granted liberty to approach the learned trial court by way of an appropriate application for referring the dispute between the Mediation Centre of District Court,
Mathura.
If such an application is being made, the said application shall be considered by the trial court in accordance with law.
